reconcile.connective: Keil & Delitzsch treat Ecclesiastes' silence as an incomplete stage of revelation that the New Testament later completes, not a rival teaching.

discrepancy.connective: Bart Ehrman argues in Heaven and Hell that Job and Ecclesiastes' finality and Daniel and Revelation's judgment are genuinely different, developing views, not one teaching.

skeptic.name: Bart D. Ehrman
skeptic.work: Heaven and Hell: A History of the Afterlife
skeptic.attribution: Bart D. Ehrman, Heaven and Hell: A History of the Afterlife (Simon & Schuster, 2020)

excerpts.excerpt_text: But that which Koheleth expresses here only in a particularly rugged way is the view of Hades predominating in the O.T. … Revelation intentionally permits this manner of viewing it to remain; but from premises which the revelation sets forth, the religious consciousness in the course of time draws always more decidedly the conclusion, that the man who is united to God will fully reach through death that which since the entrance of sin into the world cannot be reached without the loss of this present life, i.e., without death, viz., a more perfect life in fellowship with God. Yet the confusion of the O.T. representation of Hades remains; in the Book of Sirach it also still throws its deep shadows (17:22f.) into the contemplation of the future; for the first time the N.T. solution actually removes the confusion, and turns the scale in favour of the view of death on its side of light.
excerpts.on_tension_rationale: KD explicitly frames Ecclesiastes' no-afterlife anthropology as an unfinished, historically-limited stage of OT revelation of Hades that the NT 'solution' later clarifies/completes -- a progressive-revelation harmonization directly addressing the OT-vs-NT afterlife tension named in the summary.

pd_work.resource: John W. Haley, An Examination of the Alleged Discrepancies of the Bible (1874)
pd_work.author: John W. Haley
pd_work.note: Haley's 'Intermediate State' and 'Future Punishment -- Its Nature' sections (Doctrinal Discrepancies, pp. 204-219) work this exact contradiction verse-by-verse: Job 3:18, Ecclesiastes 9:5-6 and 9:10 are paired directly against Luke 16:22-23 and Revelation 14:10-11, and Daniel 12:2 is cited among the 'everlasting shame' proof-texts, with Haley's own resolution invoking progressive revelation ('revelation is progressive... those early times were the dim dawn of revelation') alongside a contextual reading limiting Ecclesiastes' scope to 'under the sun.'
